fixture declares 2 buses
fixture declares 1 line
r = 0 ohm/km -> I^2*R losses are identically zero; pandapower's residual rounding pinned at 1e-9
the single declared load (2 MW)
slack bus holds the external-grid setpoint exactly

V2 = sqrt((1 + sqrt(1 - 4*(p*x)^2)) / 2) with p = P/baseMva = 2/100 = 0.02 pu and x = Xohm/baseZ = (0.1 ohm/km * 10 km) / ((20 kV)^2 / 100 MVA) = 1 / 4 = 0.25 pu -> p*x = 5e-3 -> 4*(px)^2 = 1e-4 -> V2^2 = (1 + 0.99995)/2 = 0.999975 -> V2 = 0.9999875 (the high branch NR converges to). [An earlier draft of this derivation wrote 1/4 as 0.025 — the harness caught the 10x slip against the real engine, which is exactly its job.]

sin(delta) = p*x/V2 = 5.00000625e-3 rad = 0.28647895 degrees across the line (lossless: P = V1*V2*sin(delta)/X); bus-2 LAGS the slack reference so pandapower reports the negative angle; absTolerance 1e-4 deg absorbs NR's convergence residual (observed -0.28648367, residual 4.7e-6 deg — the solver's own tolerance, not a formula error)
I = P / (sqrt(3) * V2_LL * ...) with the SOLVED V2: 2 MW / (1.7320508 * 20 kV * 0.9999875) = 0.05773575 kA (the current reflects the actual end-of-line voltage, not the nominal)
